title: The Third Order
hookLine: laypeople who follow Francis in family and work

lines: A WHOLE TOWN WANTS TO FOLLOW.
cards: A preacher has just finished, and the whole town wants to go with him. That's the scene in the Little Flowers, in a village near Assisi called Cannara, the same chapter that tells of the birds.

Francis preaches, and the people are so moved that men and women alike want to leave their houses, their fields, their families, and follow him on the road. On paper, a preacher's dream. But Francis says no.
Don't be in a hurry, he tells them. Don't leave. I'll arrange what you should do.
There are the brothers, and Clare's sisters. What about everyone else?

teach.h: A THIRD WAY: FOLLOW WITHOUT LEAVING.
teach.b: The Little Flowers says that after Cannara, Francis began to think about a third order, for people who would follow him without leaving home. Married people. Parents.
In the early days they were called the brothers and sisters of penance, and penance there doesn't mean misery. It means turning, a whole life turned toward God.
Today the Church calls it the Secular Franciscan Order, secular meaning lived in the world, not in a cloister. Francis wrote a letter to people like this, to all the faithful living in the world.
In it he says, more or less: love God with your whole heart, love your neighbor as yourself, turn from what pulls you away, receive the Body and Blood of the Lord. Then something startling.
People who live like that, he writes, are the spouses and brothers and mothers of Jesus Christ.

teach.h: BROTHER, SISTER AND MOTHER OF CHRIST.
teach.b: He's leaning on the gospel, where Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "whosoever shall do the will of my Father, that is in heaven, he is my brother, and my sister, and my mother." Not a monk. Not a friar.
Anyone. You don't need a habit or a monastery to belong to Francis's family. The poverty looks different at home: a simpler house, a lighter grip on things, generosity with time.

teach.h: POVERTY AND PEACE AT THE KITCHEN TABLE.
teach.b: The peace looks different: a kitchen table, an office, a difficult relative.

teach.h: HE IS MY BROTHER, AND MY SISTER, AND MY MOTHER.
teach.b: Secular Franciscans make a promise, meet in local groups, and go back to their lives. The point was never to run away from ordinary life. It was to bring Francis into it.

how: Secular Franciscans are lay Catholics, single or married, who make a profession to live the gospel in the spirit of Francis, meet regularly in local fraternities, and carry that life into their families and work.

games.why: the Little Flowers says he told them not to leave, and then began to think of a third order for people in the world.

practice: Let one of these Franciscan stories choose you: patience at a closed gate, asking what the wolf is hungry for, stopping for a bird, a good thing done in secret.

Then set it somewhere specific in your ordinary day, the commute, the dishes, the call with your mother, and see yourself doing it there. If you pray, ask Francis's God for help to keep it; if not, just hold the picture steady.

wordCard.voice: Third Order. Laypeople who follow Francis without leaving home, living his gospel in family and work. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: penance, a change of heart; the early name of the Third Order was the order of penance.

carryVoice: Your line: francis at home. No habit needed to belong to his family. Go gently.
